chapter: Ann Cook session and Buddy Petit stories
title: Red Onion Drag and the old house of detention district
summary: Humphrey explains the Red Onion Drag name came from a red house behind the house of detention near James Alley, and recalls advertising wagons there.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Yeah, let me put this next one on. Uh, that was Franklin Street. Now this is the Red Onion Drag.
Uh, let me stop it for a second. Where did the name come from, Red Onion Drag?
Oh, Louis put that name right here. See, there'd be a place back, way back, uh, back behind the house of detention.
Well, they called that the Red Onion Drag. Back there, old house was painted red.
Pretty tough guy lived back there. Mm-hmm.
Where was the house of detention there?
Cleveland and, uh, I mean, uh, 290 Avenue and, uh, on the other side of Galveston, I came.
Where the Parish Prison is now? Around in there?
Yeah. Just about where it is now.
Where on James Alley and that?
Yeah, James Alley. And that's in the James Alley. You go across there. Then you get into James Alley. Tough part back there.
Mm-hmm. Let me put it on again.

Well, see, we used to advertise on back there. Mm-hmm. On Sunday. And, God, you know, saw a little scrap or something like that. Mm-hmm. Well, we never paid no time to that. We'd get off the wagon and go and get our drink and get back on there. And there'd be scrappings going on. We'd pay another and pull off. Whole time, right? Rip them up. Rip them up Joe. Mm-hmm.
